thread:
sam: seeing a surge of apiserver 5xxs in eu-west-3 starting ~10:12 UTC, controller-manager restarted a few times and leader changed twice. GPU provisioner jobs are piling up. Anyone else? :rotating_light:

infra-bot: [ALERT] apiserver_5xx_rate > 4.5% (3m) in eu-west-3. controller-manager restarts: 12 in 15m. failed jobs: gpu-provisioner (x46). Related traces: traces.redwood/gpuprov/eu-west-3

maya: looking now. quick glance at network metrics — egress SNAT utilization high for nat-gw-eu-3a/b. pulling conntrack/timeout stats.

sam: attaching two quick snippets from the kube-apiserver logs around the first errors:```
E1020 10:12:14.123 apiserver.go:345] error proxying to backend: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed
E1020 10:12:16.987 apiserver.go:367] dial tcp 10.50.14.22:2379: i/o timeout
```

jessica: this smells like conntrack / SNAT port exhaustion. I SSHed to one of the NAT instances and ran conntrack -S — counters are near limit.```
root@nat-gw-eu-3a:~# conntrack -S
entries: 124992 max: 131072
hashes: 16384 table-size: 262144
```

liam: yup. SNAT pool for that region is saturated. Quick mitigation options: 1) increase nf_conntrack_max on nodes, 2) widen ip_local_port_range on the controlplane NAT hosts, 3) request neteng to expand NAT pool. We should also consider routing low-priority GPU provisioning to a fallback region for the next hour. Thoughts?

maya: agree with liam. quick band-aid is sysctl bump on the NAT hosts and controllers (conntrack_max + port range). but we need neteng to expand the pool or failover the NAT Gateways. Also controller-manager restarts likely caused by transient connection failures to etcd — leases lost -> leader reselection. That explains the rollouts.

oncall: if we can avoid a full restart of controller-manager we'd prefer that. Can we quiesce the gpu-provisioner queue to reduce conntrack pressure? Maybe pause the job controller or scale it down temporarily.

sam: i can scale down the gpu-provisioner controller to 0 for 5m to drain backlog and reduce new outbound connections. executing:```
kubectl -n infra scale deployment/gpu-provisioner --replicas=0 && sleep 300 && kubectl scale deployment/gpu-provisioner --replicas=3 -n infra
```

jessica: also pushing the quick sysctl patch to NAT hosts in eu-west-3 now:`sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` and `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="15000 61000"` — will monitor counters.

liam: filing neteng ticket to expand the SNAT pool and to check HA failover on nat-gw-eu-3b. Ticket: NET-9421 (pinging @neteng).

maya: for resiliency long-term: 1) add sticky routing for controller-to-etcd controlplane to reduce ephemeral SNAT usage; 2) implement backpressure in gpu-provisioner so it respects an API 429/5xx circuit for a short window; 3) add synthetic probe for SNAT utilization into controlplane SLOs.

oncall: agree on backpressure. also recommend we add a transient policy to reroute low-priority provisioning to eu-west-1 for next 30m to catch up — acceptable cost tradeoff?

sam: approved to fall back to eu-west-1 for low-priority jobs. I'll run a canary for 50 jobs then open a broader switch if good.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1547. Severity: P2. Assigned: eng-sre oncall. Links: https://inc.redwood/INC-2026-1547, grafana: https://grafana.redwood/d/euwest3/apiserver

jessica: conntrack entries dropped after sysctl bump:```
entries: 81234 max: 262144
```

sam: controller-manager stopped flapping after scaling down provisioner and the sysctl change. continuing to watch for 30m. prepping postmortem draft, will include timeline and action items. :thumbsup:

liam: neteng acknowledged NET-9421 and started NAT pool increase.

maya: adding follow-ups: config change for gpu-provisioner backpressure + synthetic SNAT alert + runbook update for NAT saturation. assigning to @jessica for immediate runbook edits.

oncall: thanks team. monitoring. update in 15. :eyes:
